solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Famous player responsible for graffiti in the gents?

parts.note: the gents is a men's public lavatory, which British slang calls the bog
graffiti is daubed artwork, loosely art

explanation.surface: A question about who scrawls on the walls of a men's toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: BOG is British slang for a toilet, so toilet-wall graffiti is 'bog art'.
explanation.definitionFit: Humphrey Bogart was a celebrated Hollywood actor, and a player is an actor.

clue.text: Bright at first but showery later

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word but

parts.note: showery weather is rainy

explanation.surface: A weather forecast: sunny in the morning, showers later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bright' looks like part of the forecast but is the definition, meaning intelligent.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright in the sense of clever or intelligent.

clue.text: Rich American worried when kidnapped by heartless gangsters

indicators.note: kidnapped by means the worried word is held inside the gangsters' remains
heartless strips away all the middle of gangsters, leaving the ends

parts.note: to ate, as in what's eating you, is to worry

explanation.surface: A wealthy American frets after being seized by mobsters.
explanation.walkthrough: ATE for worried comes from the idiom 'what's eating you?'; 'heartless' and 'kidnapped by' do the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Gates, Microsoft's founder, is one of the wealthiest people in the United States.

clue.text: Travelled again and came back

parts.note: the prefix re- means again
plied means travelled regularly, as a ferry plies a route

explanation.surface: Someone made the journey a second time and returned.
explanation.definitionFit: Came back in the sense of answered or retorted.

clue.text: Swimmer crossing river with little energy … needing this?

definitions.text: Swimmer crossing river with little energy … needing this?

indicators.note: crossing means the swimmer's word straddles the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: a bather is someone swimming
E, the symbol for energy, is energy in little

explanation.surface: A tired swimmer making it across a river would want a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: a swimmer short of energy needs a pause.
explanation.definitionFit: A short rest to recover is a pause that lets one get one's wind back.

clue.text: Overtired? A gin is enough to get you full of energy again

indicators.note: is enough, as in enough to upset you, signals the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: If you are exhausted, one gin will perk you up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is enough' rearranges OVERTIRED and A GIN together.
explanation.definitionFit: Reinvigorated means given fresh vigour, revived.

clue.text: He rates new source of timber

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A man grading a fresh supply of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree of the genus Fraxinus yields tough, pale hardwood.

clue.text: Courage shown by police officer in control

indicators.note: in places the officer inside the word for control

parts.note: to harness something is to control it
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A police officer in charge shows bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardiness is toughness and robustness, a kind of resilience close to courage.

clue.text: International team broke records at start of season

indicators.note: broke means the word records is smashed into a new order
at start of takes the first letter of season

explanation.surface: A sports team from abroad set new records early in the season.
explanation.definitionFit: The humanitarian movement operates worldwide, a team of aid workers across nations.

clue.text: Pour wine to accompany an Italian food selection

indicators.note: to accompany puts the pour-and-wine pieces alongside the little word an, after it

parts.note: to tip a jug is to pour from it
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: Serve some wine alongside an Italian assortment of starters.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasti are the assorted Italian starters served before the pasta course.

clue.text: Sound bored, eating kind girl's special food?

indicators.note: eating means the sigh swallows the other pieces

parts.note: a sigh is the noise a bored person makes
nature means kind or sort, as in things of that nature
Di's: Di is a girl's name, with the possessive giving the S

explanation.surface: Sighing with boredom while eating some nice girl's special food.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant's speciality, the meal a chef is known for, is special food.

clue.text: Cruel king — chief character in story — died

parts.note: a hero is the protagonist of a tale
D is the usual abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: A tale's villainous monarch, the lead figure, meets his death.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical ruler of Judea who ordered the massacre of the innocents is the byword for royal cruelty.

clue.text: No cut of beef's good for eating

parts.note: shin is a cut of beef from the lower leg

explanation.surface: A judgement that no cut of beef is fit to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is informal British slang for food, so noshing is tucking in.

clue.text: Scale back limit on velocity

indicators.note: back tells us to read the following run of pieces from right to left

parts.note: to rein in is to limit, and a rein is a check
RE means on or about, as in a letter heading
V is the physics symbol for velocity

explanation.surface: An instruction to cut back a speed limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the whole run REIN, RE, V to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A vernier is a small sliding auxiliary scale for reading fine measurements.

clue.text: Fantastic new deal — single attachment for camera

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something wildly fanciful, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A salesman's pitch: a terrific bargain on one camera accessory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fantastic' rearranges NEW DEAL and SINGLE together.
explanation.definitionFit: A lens with a broad field of view that photographers fit to their cameras.

clue.text: Aggressor getting close to target over Germany

parts.note: in hide-and-seek a searcher getting close is told they are getting warm
on means over, on top of

explanation.surface: An attacker closing on a target above the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: Dac wrote 'Germany'; the editor changed it to 'Gulf' in the printed clue, which leaves the parse broken.
explanation.definitionFit: A warmonger is someone who stirs up war, a belligerent person.

clue.text: Surprisingly assert there's place within for stationery items

indicators.note: within says the place abbreviation goes inside
surprisingly means the word assert turns up in an unexpected order

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: A surprised claim that there is room for some office items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'place' reads as part of the surface phrase 'there's place', but it is the abbreviation PL; 'Surprisingly' gives STAERS and 'within' houses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Devices for fastening papers together are office and stationery equipment.

clue.text: Not all the barracks will accommodate sappers?

indicators.note: will accommodate means the little word the houses the soldiers inside it

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are the army's sappers
quarters are soldiers' lodgings, as barracks are

explanation.surface: Not every bit of the barracks will house the engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Three-quarters of something falls short of the whole, a large fraction rather than everything.

clue.text: Distinguished English artist linked to Ernst, oddly

parts.note: Tracey Emin is an English artist

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of Ernst

explanation.surface: A notable English painter is associated with Max Ernst, strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent means famous and respected in one's field.

clue.text: Contacted me over deal I struck

indicators.note: over in a down clue turns the word me upside down
struck means the letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone got in touch about a deal I made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns ME to EM; 'struck' rearranges DEAL I to AILED.
explanation.definitionFit: To send someone a message electronically is to contact them.

clue.text: Extract from Leone western most recently released?

indicators.note: Extract from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A clip from Sergio Leone's latest cowboy film.
explanation.definitionFit: The latest, most recent thing out is the freshest.

clue.text: Word for short, tight-fisted type

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a miser is a tight-fisted person

explanation.surface: A term for a stingy person, in brief.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving one's word is making a pledge or vow.

clue.text: Portion of money putting husband in ecstatic state

indicators.note: in places the husband's letter inside the ecstatic state

parts.note: a trance is a rapt or ecstatic state

explanation.surface: Getting a share of the cash sends the husband into raptures.
explanation.definitionFit: A tranche is an instalment or slice of a sum of money, as in a loan paid in stages.

clue.text: Dishonest person getting work in African country

parts.note: a con is a confidence trickster
to go is to work or function, as a machine does

explanation.surface: A swindler finds a job in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Republic of the Congo is a nation in central Africa.

clue.text: Standard golf score

definitions.meaning: a Roman legion's standard was a bird emblem carried on a pole
two under par on a single hole in golf

explanation.definitionFit: Both the Roman legion's banner and two-under-par on a golf hole take this bird's name.

clue.text: Not working? Local church will collect money to help those affected

indicators.note: will collect means the pub takes the money in

parts.note: a local is a British pub, and an inn is one
the dole is British state benefit paid to the unemployed
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The neighbourhood church raises funds for victims of unemployment.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: 'Not working?' stands for the state of idleness, the question mark admitting the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Laziness, the habit of avoiding work, is the state the definition hints at.

clue.text: Prison sentence a year? Of variable length, perhaps

parts.note: a stretch is slang for a term in prison
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Is a jail term of one year or open-ended?
explanation.definitionFit: Something elastic can be pulled to different lengths.

clue.text: Clever, being a doctor? There's nothing to it

parts.note: O, the zero shape, means nothing

explanation.surface: Is being a physician easy, with nothing much to it?
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful and deft, much as clever does.
